answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with staked identity: docking a locked bond at a shared jetty grants admission, and a cipher signature binds that bond to one unclonable key. Votes weigh by bond, not by name count, so a thousand fake wallets still cast their owner's single vote. To take a quorum an attacker must lock more capital than all honest agents combined — about 5.1M tokens of a 10M pool — a public, slashable deposit. A bridge between registries refuses to relay attestations for bonds absent from the jetty, so a counterfeit fleet cannot farm one deposit twice.
